On his desk, among jade seals, lies a plain bronze bell-clapper, the kind a valley smith would make. The Ha name. The Keeper's brother "climbed the easy way, up a cloud."

choices.text: Mention a bell-caster who sits on the step of the Tower

effects.log: The Elder's brush stops for half a breath, then goes on writing.

choices.text: Say nothing, and take your leave

effects.log: You leave the Ninth Pavilion with the question still in your mouth.

events.text: Ha Mu-gyeol sends for you. "You spoke of a bell-caster," he says. "I had no sibling. Heaven took me from no one. I was found on a cloud with a gift and nothing else." He smiles the way the court smiles. "Do not repeat that story. Rootless people do not build towers. They cast bells, and die."

effects.log: Something moves behind the Elder's calm, like a fish under ice. He dismisses you.
You bow. The Elder thanks you, and you see his hand close over the clapper.

events.text: Late at night you pass the Ninth Pavilion and its door is open. Ha Mu-gyeol sits alone with the bronze clapper in his hands, and he is weeping, without a sound, the way someone weeps who has not done it for ten thousand years and has forgotten how loud it is supposed to be.

choices.text: Go in and sit with him

effects.log: You sit. He does not send you away. After a long time he says, "They were older. They carried me on their back to the testing."

choices.text: Close the door softly and keep watch outside

effects.log: You keep the door until dawn. Nobody else sees an Elder of the Jade Court weep.

events.text: Ha Mu-gyeol finds you at the edge of the clouds and puts the bronze clapper in your hand. "Carry it down," he says. "I cannot go. I am too high now, and too late. But you climb. If you ever reach the top, give it a bell." He does not say whose. He does not need to.

choices.text: Promise to carry it to the top

effects.log: You take the clapper. It is heavier than bronze should be.

choices.text: Ask him to come with you

effects.log: "Not this life," says Mu-gyeol, and for a moment he sounds exactly like someone else.

events.text: A herald of your pantheon kneels at your door with a sealed order. The Tower of Trials still answers to no one, not even the gods, and your pantheon is tired of it. "Take the Tower for us," the order reads. "Climb it, and hold its top in our name. Bring us the answer at its summit." The seal is still warm.

choices.text: Obey: take the banner and go

effects.log: You take the pantheon's banner and go down to the Tower with it on your back.

choices.text: Refuse: the Tower is not anyone's to take

effects.log: You hand the order back unopened. By evening every hall in heaven knows.

choices.text: Say you will climb it, but only as a climber

effects.log: You promise to climb, and promise nothing else. The herald does not know what to write down.

events.text: You come to the Tower with your pantheon's banner and command the door to open in its name. It does not. You command louder. It does not. Behind you other climbers start to smile. The Keeper, sweeping, does not look up. "They knocked as rulers," they say. "I only open for climbers." In heaven, by evening, they are laughing at you.

choices.text: Put the banner down and climb as one climber

effects.log: You lean the banner against the wall and climb. The door opens at once. The pantheon is not told.

choices.text: Go back and report the failure

effects.log: You report it, word for word. Your pantheon will not look at you for a decade.
You strike the door with a god's whole strength. It does not even notice. Your hand aches for a year.

events.text: The scandal of your refusal runs through every golden road. Gods who have never spoken to you stop you to ask if it is true. Some are furious. Some, quietly, are not: a minor god of harvests presses your hand and whispers, "I climbed it once. Floor six. Thank you for saying it out loud."

effects.log: You stand by it. Your pantheon cools toward you; the gods of small things warm.

choices.text: Smooth it over with your pantheon

effects.log: You make apologies you do not mean. The pantheon accepts them; nobody believes them.

events.text: You climb as one climber among many: a mortal from a far province, a beast-tamer, a nervous young immortal. On floor three a mortal with no root at all gives you a hand up a broken stair without knowing what you are. The Keeper, below, does not bow to you. You are glad of it.

choices.text: Thank the mortal and climb beside them a while

effects.log: You climb beside them for three floors. They never learn who you are. It is the best year of your godhood.
They laugh and do not believe you. "Then climb faster, Your Divinity," they say.

events.text: The climber on the stair ahead wears faded blue and carries a sword far older than its owner. {npc} is the last heir of a sword clan of Hubei that fell three generations ago, and bows to you with a formality nobody has used in a hundred years. "I must restore my house's name by the fiftieth floor," {he} says. "Please do not take it personally when I pass you."

effects.log: {npc} looks startled, then pleased, and hides it badly.
{npc} tries, all that year. It is an honest race.

events.text: You share a landing with {npc} for a night. {He} cleans the old sword for an hour by the light of a small fire, talking only about technique. Then, very late, {he} says, "My father failed at the Mirror Floors. My father came home and never picked up a sword again. Everyone said it was shame." {He} does not look at you. "It was not shame."

effects.log: "My father saw something in the mirror that nobody could live beside," says {npc}. "I want to know what."

choices.text: Share a story of your own

effects.log: You trade a story for a story. By morning the formality between you has worn a little thin.

events.text: On the bronze floors you find {npc} kneeling before a mirror, the old sword across {his} knees. In the bronze stands a man in faded blue, weeping: {his} father. "Father did not fail," {npc} whispers. "Father gave up the floor to carry a stranger down, told no one, and let them call it shame."

mem.note: knelt with me at the mirror

effects.log: You kneel together until the mirror is only a mirror. {npc} stands up lighter than {he} knelt.

choices.text: Tell {him} the clan's name is not worth this

effects.log: "It is all I have," {npc} says, and climbs on alone, faster, too fast.
You climb past. Behind you, the sound of a sword laid down on bronze.

events.text: The fiftieth floor is close, and {npc} is not ready, and knows it. "Swear brotherhood with me," {he} says, holding out the hilt of the old sword. "Or race me to the fiftieth, and let the better one restore a name. Either way, I am done climbing alone."

choices.text: Swear brotherhood on the old sword

mem.note: sworn brotherhood on the old sword

effects.log: You swear. {npc} weeps once, briefly, and is embarrassed about it for a week.
You race. You win the fiftieth. {npc} bows to you, formally, and becomes your rival for life.

choices.text: Tell {him} to go first and push harder

effects.log: "Harder," you say. {npc} nods, and takes the stairs at a run.

events.text: Word comes down the stairs that {npc} went to the fiftieth floor before {he} was ready, because someone told {him} to push harder. {npc} dies on the fiftieth floor, before the jade scales, the old sword still in {his} hand. The Keeper brings the sword down and lays it across the lowest step.

choices.text: Carry the sword to the fiftieth floor yourself

effects.npcPass: on the fiftieth floor of the Tower, before the jade scales
effects.log: You carry it up and set it on the scales. They balance, for once, perfectly.

effects.npcPass: on the fiftieth floor of the Tower, before the jade scales
effects.log: You climb. You do not look at the step.

events.text: {npc} comes to you at the foot of the stair with the old sword wrapped in silk, and kneels. "I watched you at the mirror, and on the stairs," {he} says. "My house can wait. Take me as your disciple. I would rather learn from someone who climbs like you than restore a name that never climbed at all."

mem.note: took me as a disciple on the stair

effects.log: You accept. {npc} unwraps the sword and lays it at your feet, the old way.

choices.text: Refuse gently: restore your name first

mem.note: sent me back to my name

effects.log: {npc} bows. "Then I will come back with it restored," {he} says, and does, years later, with a smile.

events.text: Someone is sitting on the rail of the stair, swinging {his} feet over a drop of a hundred floors, a crescent blade across {his} lap: {npc}, a prodigy of the Heavenly Demon line, who grins at you with every tooth. "I never lie," {he} says. "So: I mean to reach the top before you, and I will use you if it helps. Want to make a deal?"

effects.log: "One floor at a time," says {npc}. "Help on this one, knives on the next. Fair?"
"Polite!" {npc} laughs. "I like you already. That is bad news for you."

mem.note: tried to push me off the rail

effects.log: {npc} catches the rail one-handed and swings back up, delighted. "Now you are interesting."

events.text: {npc} drops onto your landing with a new deal. "The Scales are close. I am going to steal their verdict: weigh my deeds while the judge is busy with yours. You will not even notice. I am only telling you because I never lie."

effects.log: The judge notices at once. {npc} is thrown down three floors, laughing all the way.
{npc} is caught before {he} starts. "Fair," {he} says. "I would have done it to you."

mem.note: offered to help steal the verdict

effects.log: "Oh, no," says {npc}. "You would only be good at it. Go away."

events.text: In the golden arrays {npc} solves half a lock and waits for you to turn the other half. You turn it. The floor folds, and you are on the stairs below, alone, and {npc} is above, waving. "I said knives on the next floor," {he} calls down. "I never lie. Nothing personal."

effects.log: You laugh. You climb. You are, somehow, not angry, and that makes {npc} frown for the first time.
"Good," says {npc} from above. "I only respect people who beat me. Try."

events.text: You catch {npc} at last on a landing and fight {him}, properly, with nothing held back on either side. When it is over {npc} is sitting against the wall with {his} blade across the floor, grinning up at you. "There," {he} says. "Now I respect you. That is all I ever wanted. Ally?"

mem.note: beat me, then shook my hand

effects.log: {npc} shakes on it. For the rest of the climb nobody gets near either of you.
"Fair," {npc} says to your back. "I would have."

events.text: The storm floors come for {npc} and you together, and the ninth bolt is meant for you. {npc} steps into it on purpose, still grinning. "I never lie," {he} says. "So I will tell you: I wanted to see what that felt like." {npc} dies in the storm, smiling, the crescent blade still bright.

choices.text: Carry {his} blade up to the next floor

effects.npcPass: in the storm floors of the Tower, taking a bolt meant for another
effects.log: You carry the crescent blade up into the clean light after the storm.

choices.text: Stand in the rain a long time

effects.npcPass: in the storm floors of the Tower, taking a bolt meant for another
effects.log: You stand in the rain until the floor lets you go.

events.text: A monk with a lantern and a string of prayer beads is climbing slowly, as if every step were a prayer. {npc} is from a small mountain temple, and is climbing for someone else. "My friend died in the Tower," {he} says. "Their soul is caught in the silver scrolls of the sixtieth floor. I am going to bring them out."

effects.log: {npc} bows over the lantern. "Then there are three of us," {he} says. "My friend counts."

choices.text: Ask if that can be done

mem.note: asked if it could be done

effects.log: "No one has done it," says {npc}. "That is not the same as cannot."

events.text: {npc} has stopped on a landing to share {his} rice with a climber who fell. {He} looks up at you. "I could be three floors higher," {he} says, "if I stopped stopping." {He} laughs at {him}self. "My friend would hit me with this lantern if I did."

mem.note: stopped with me for a stranger

effects.log: You help {npc} bind the fallen climber's ankle. It costs you the year. You do not mind.

choices.text: Climb on, and save a place at the top

effects.log: "Save it well," says {npc}. "I am slow."

events.text: In the silver archive {npc} finds the scroll. {He} holds it to {his} chest and cannot open it. "If I read it, I will know how they died," {he} says. "If I do not, I cannot guide them out." {His} lantern is shaking.

effects.log: You read it together. It is a short scroll. At the end {npc} smiles, and a light walks out of the shelves beside {him}.

choices.text: Read it for {him}, and tell {him} only the good part

effects.log: You read it and tell {npc} only the good part. The light comes out. {npc} never asks about the rest.

mem.note: told me to leave my friend

effects.log: {npc} puts the scroll back. Something in {his} face goes hard, and stays that way.

events.text: {npc} comes down the stair with a light walking beside {him}. "I have what I came for," {he} says. "And you are stuck below the next guardian." {He} puts the lantern in your hands. "Take my climb. I have no more use for it. Every floor I would have stood on, stand on for me."

mem.note: took my lantern and my climb

effects.log: You take it. {npc} and the light go down the stairs together, and out of the Tower, and you climb on with a lantern that never goes out.

choices.text: Refuse, and send {him} home with it

mem.note: sent me home with the lantern

effects.log: "Then I will light it in the temple for you," says {npc}. "Every night until you reach the top."

events.text: {npc} still climbs, but not for anyone now. {He} does not bow to other climbers any more, and {his} lantern has gone out. "The Tower took them and kept them," {he} says. "Heaven did not answer. Why would it answer you?"

choices.text: "Maybe it will not. I am climbing anyway."

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long time. Then {he} lights the lantern again from your fire, without a word.
{npc} climbs on in the dark. You hear {him} on the stairs above for years.

events.text: {npc} has a satchel full of rumours and an abacus that clicks while {he} talks. The child of a Shandong merchant guild, {he} is climbing the Tower mostly to sell things to people who are climbing the Tower. "Floor rumours," {he} says. "Which stair creaks, which echo cheats. Forty taels. Friends get a discount. We are not friends yet."

choices.text: Buy a rumour for forty taels

effects.log: The rumour is true, and exact, and worth more than forty taels. {npc} winks.

choices.text: Ask what it takes to be friends

effects.log: "A promise kept," says {npc}. "Nobody in the Tower has managed it yet."
"You will be back," says {npc}, clicking the abacus.

events.text: {npc} is in trouble. {He} owes a sect of the Hushed Lantern four hundred taels for rumours that turned out false, and two of them are on the landing below, smiling. "I need you to promise me something," {npc} says quickly. "Promise you will not tell them I am up here. That is all."

effects.log: You keep the promise when they come asking. {npc} stares at you afterwards like you are a rare coin.
You pay the debt with your own money. {npc} cannot speak for a whole floor.
You tell them. {npc} looks down at you from the stairs, and nods, slowly, as if writing it in a ledger.

events.text: {npc} slides a pouch across the step to you. "Everything I know about the next ten floors," {he} says. "Free. You kept your word, and nobody does that in here." {He} looks embarrassed. "It is the first thing I have ever given away. I do not like how it feels. I think I will do it again."

choices.text: Take it, and give {him} something back

effects.log: You give {npc} the best thing you have. It is not worth much. {He} keeps it for the rest of {his} life.
The rumours are perfect. You climb ten floors as if you had climbed them before.

events.text: At the next guardian floor everyone waiting knows your weakness: the side you guard too much, the breath you take before you strike. Someone has been selling it. Across the landing {npc} will not meet your eyes. "Business," {he} says. "You taught me what a promise is worth."

choices.text: Take the floor anyway, with a new habit

effects.log: You change the habit there and then. It is the hardest year of your climb, and the best.
You have it out. {npc} does not run. At the end {he} says, "We are even," and you both know you are not.

events.text: {npc} is going home. The satchel is heavy with silver and the abacus has stopped clicking. "I quit," {he} says. "Rich. Twenty-two floors and a fortune. The Tower is a terrible place to climb and a wonderful place to sell things." {He} presses a small jade token into your hand. "For the top. Do not sell it."

effects.log: You keep it. Years later, at the top, you will find it still in your sleeve.
You walk {npc} to the gate. The Keeper sells {him} a cup of cold tea, and {npc} pays, laughing.

events.text: A huge climber in furs is wrestling a bronze practice post on the landing and winning. {npc} is a wrestler of the Khaganate steppe, loud, generous, fearless, who sees the Tower as a horse to break. "I only want the Beast Cages," {he} roars. "The rest is stairs! Climb with me, small one, or get out of my way!"

effects.log: {npc} slaps your back hard enough to move you a floor. "Good! We eat together tonight."
You wrestle. You lose, or you win; either way {npc} laughs so loudly the bells ring.

events.text: At night on a landing a great grey wolf comes up the stair, a wolf no one let in, and lies down beside {npc}. "The Khaganate's grey wolf," {he} says softly, for once. "It came all this way to watch me. My grandfather said it only comes to people who will do something foolish and brave." {He} scratches its ears. "Swear brotherhood with me?"

choices.text: Swear, with the wolf as witness

effects.log: You swear. The grey wolf stands, looks at you both, and goes back down the stairs.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will be {his} friend, not {his} brother

effects.log: "Friend is good," {npc} says, a little hurt. "Brother is better. I will wait."

events.text: In the iron cages {npc} meets the great ox-bear of the fortieth floor, old and slow and mossy-horned, and {his} eyes light up. "Now that is a horse to break." The warden says win without hurting it. {npc} says nothing. {He} cracks {his} knuckles.

choices.text: Stand with {him} and wrestle it gently

mem.note: wrestled the beast with me, gently

effects.log: The two of you wrestle the old beast to its knees without a scratch. The warden bows. {npc} weeps, loudly, with joy.
{npc} goes at it full strength. The ox-bear goes at {him} the same way.
{npc} throws you off and goes in anyway, angry with you for the first time.

events.text: Mercy failed in the iron cages. {npc} would not hurt the old beast and would not give up, and the beast did not understand. {npc} dies on the fortieth floor with {his} arms still around the ox-bear's neck, as if holding a friend. The ox-bear has not moved from {his} side since.

effects.npcPass: on the fortieth floor of the Tower, arms around the old ox-bear
effects.log: You sit with the beast all year. On the last day it gets up and lets you pass.

effects.npcPass: on the fortieth floor of the Tower, arms around the old ox-bear
effects.log: You send word. In the spring a grey wolf is seen at the foot of the Tower, howling.

events.text: You fall on a floor above the cages, badly, and {npc} finds you. {He} picks you up like a lamb and carries you down a whole floor, singing a steppe song so loudly the echoes complain. "There," {he} says at the landing. "Now I go home. I broke the horse. The steppe will make a song of it. You will be in the song, small one."

effects.log: {npc} sings the whole song. It is very long, and you are in it, three times, mostly falling.
{npc} goes home a hero. Years later a steppe herder in your province sings you the song without knowing it is yours.

events.text: The youngest commander of the imperial guard climbs in black-and-gold armour with a sealed order in {his} sleeve. {npc} is cold, exact, and does not pretend otherwise. "The throne ordered me to climb beside you and measure you," {he} says. "I will report everything. I thought you should know. It is the only courtesy I am allowed."

effects.log: {npc} blinks. People do not often thank {him}. "You are welcome," {he} says, stiffly.
You climb a floor at full strength in front of {him}. {npc} writes it down, and does not hide that {he} is impressed.

events.text: On a landing {npc} takes off the black-and-gold helmet for the first time. "Two years ago I was ordered to close a village gate during a plague," {he} says. "I closed it. I followed the order. The Tower shows it to me every floor." {He} does not ask for anything. That is how you know it is a confession.

effects.log: "The hand was mine," says {npc}. But {he} sleeps that night, which {he} has not done in a year.

choices.text: Tell {him} the Tower is right to show it

effects.log: {npc} nods. "Yes. It is." {He} puts the helmet back on.

events.text: On the jade floors {npc} arrests you. There is an old warrant, from the throne, for something you did or did not do. "I have the order," {he} says, and {his} hand is not quite steady on the seal. "I have always followed the order."

mem.note: held out their wrists to me

effects.log: You hold out your wrists. {npc} looks at them for a long time, then tears the warrant in half. "Not today," {he} says.
You fight on the jade scales, and they weigh you both. {npc} loses, and goes down the stairs to report it.
You strike while {npc} hesitates over the seal. {He} falls down three floors. The Tower remembers.

events.text: {npc} has burned the sealed order. "I have stopped reporting," {he} says. "I am done with orders. I will guard one stair, my own choice, so you can get past it." On the floor above, the shadows are already coming down. {npc} draws and plants {his} feet.

choices.text: Climb past and trust {him} to hold

effects.log: You climb. {npc} holds the stair. {npc} dies holding the stair, sword up, and nothing passes {him}.
You hold it together. You both live. {npc} looks at you as if you had broken a rule {he} had never heard of.

events.text: {npc} kneels to you on the stair in full black-and-gold, as the guard kneels to the throne, and you understand {he} has heard who you are outside the Tower. "I was sent to measure you," {he} says. "I have measured. If you ever want a house set on the throne, or kept on it, send for me."

effects.log: You accept. Years later, when crowns are argued over, {npc} will be in the room, measuring.
"That is an order," {npc} says, smiling for the first time. "I will follow it."

events.text: A god of war is climbing the Tower: {npc}, with spear-scarred hands and a voice used to being obeyed by armies. {He} is furious to be starting at floor one, like a mortal. "Race me," {he} says. "Floor by floor. When I reach the top first, I will tell Heaven I was the answer all along."

effects.log: {npc} takes the stairs three at a time and is thrown back by the first floor for showing off.

choices.text: Tell {him} the first floor wants humility

mem.note: warned me about the first floor

effects.log: {npc} laughs at you. The first floor throws {him} down the stairs. {He} stops laughing.

events.text: {npc} has been stuck on floor six for a year, the floor of dust and patience. {He} has broken nine brooms. "A god of war," {he} says through {his} teeth, "sweeping." The Keeper, far below, is smiling.

effects.log: You sweep beside the war god until {his} shoulders unclench. On the last day {he} laughs, once, at {him}self.
{npc} watches you pass. Something in {his} pride cracks and does not mend.

events.text: The war god catches you on the storm floors and the race is close at last. On the cloud-stair {npc} stops. "In heaven I have never lost," {he} says. "Here I have lost to dust, to a broom, to you. I do not understand why I feel better." {He} holds out a spear-scarred hand.

choices.text: Take it: climb the rest as allies

mem.note: climbed beside me as an ally

effects.log: You climb on together. A war god who has learned to lose is a frightening ally.
{npc} grins like a soldier. "To the end, then." It is the best race either of you ever ran.

events.text: {npc} was a god once and is not now: a domain lost, a temple pulled down, a name nobody prays to. {He} climbs in a worn robe that was golden once. "I am going to the top to ask for it back," {he} says. "My name. My river. They took them in a war in heaven I did not even fight."

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as if no one had offered {him} anything in a thousand years.

choices.text: Ask what the river was called

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It is a beautiful name. You are the first to say it aloud in an age.

events.text: On the mirror floors {npc} sees {him}self as a god again, crowned and worshipped, and stands before it a whole year. "I could stay here," {he} says. "The mirror gives it back. Isn't that the same thing?"

effects.log: {npc} weeps, then turns {his} back on the mirror. It cracks behind {him}.
You leave {npc} with the crown that is not there. Years later {he} is still standing in front of it.

events.text: {npc} stops on the white jade floors and laughs. "I do not want it back," {he} says, amazed. "The river, the name. I wanted someone to remember it. You did." {He} takes off the worn golden robe and leaves it on the stair. "I think I will be a climber. It is the best domain I have ever held."

effects.log: You climb on together, two former somethings, toward the light.

choices.text: Take the robe up a floor for {him}

effects.log: You carry the old robe one floor higher and hang it on a bell. It looks well there.

events.text: {npc} is a god who does not say which god. {He} climbs quietly and asks the Keeper's name of everyone on the landings. "There is an answer at the top," {he} says to you. "A builder asked why only the gifted may climb. I want the answer for myself. Gods should not have to ask."

effects.log: {npc} has no reply. It bothers {him} for three floors.

choices.text: Tell {him} the Keeper's name is not for sale

effects.log: "Everything is for sale above the clouds," says {npc}. "That is the trouble."

events.text: {npc} has found a way, {he} says: an array that would carry {him} past the silence floors, straight to the door, with the answer taken instead of earned. "Come with me," {he} says. "We can share it. Why climb the last floors at all?"

choices.text: Refuse: the answer is not a thing

effects.log: "Then what is it?" {npc} asks. You climb on without answering. {He} follows, slowly.
The array carries you both to a door of light. It does not open. You wake on the stairs, a year older.

mem.note: broke my array while I slept

effects.log: You break it. {npc} wakes and looks at you as at a thief. The Tower remembers that, too.

events.text: At the edge of the mist {npc} sits down on a step. "I understand now," {he} says. "The answer cannot be carried. It is not at the top. It is the climbing." {He} laughs, softly. "Even gods stopped somewhere. That is why we are gods, and not the answer."

choices.text: Sit with {him} at the edge of the mist

mem.note: sat with me at the mist

effects.log: You sit with a god who has stopped wanting to be one. It is very quiet.

Heaven seems to find that the best answer of all. It has not known for ten thousand years either.

events.text: From the Spire you can see every world at once: the provinces below, the small worlds that float, the realms above the clouds. To the west, through the seam, there is a grey stone tower, and a small lantern burning in it. Beside you stands a second door, facing west, in grey stone, a stonewright's mark beside the letters from the golden arrays.

choices.text: Lay a hand on the west door

effects.log: The stone is warm. Nothing opens yet. Somewhere, someone on the other side felt that.
"Tamsin keeps the other gate of this same Tower," the Keeper said once, freed. "I never saw it. You could."

choices.text: Look at the lantern a long time

effects.log: The lantern bobs, as if someone holding it had turned to look back at you.

events.text: At the west door of the Spire someone is waiting, sitting on the grey stone sill with their boots crossed: the friend from the other sky you swore kinship with in the Tower. They grin as if no time had passed. "Come and see my world one day," they say. A line of light runs round the door. The road to your friend's world will open soon. But crossing has a price.

effects.log: "The world you leave forgets you," your friend says quietly. "Every name, every grave. Only the Tower remembers. That is what it means, to be the one it remembers."
You clasp hands across the sill. Their hand is warm, and real, and a little cold at the fingertips, like stone.

choices.text: Say you are not ready to be forgotten

effects.log: "Nobody is," says your friend. "Take your time. The door is patient. So am I."

events.text: A scroll is waiting on the top step of the Spire, in a careful bell-caster's hand: your soul, in a few lines. {tw_climbs} climbs in the Tower, counting every life. The {tw_best} floor, and then the last. Who climbed beside you; what the guardians said to you last. And at the bottom: "The dust will miss you. I will not. I will be too busy being small."

effects.log: You keep it. The last line makes you laugh every time, and then not.

choices.text: Leave it for the next climber to find

effects.log: You leave it on the step. Let the next one see that it can be done.

events.text: Heaven speaks once more from the Spire, softly: "Sit with me a while. Watch one of them climb." And far below, in a valley with no name, you see a small child with soot on their face casting a little bell for fun, and laughing when it comes out flat.

effects.log: You sit with Heaven and watch the child. The bell is flat. They hang it anyway.

choices.text: Wish the child well and go down

effects.log: You wish them a good, ordinary, small life, and go down the stairs into your own.
